# doze

> doze runs your whole local development stack as native processes on macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux, with no Docker and no VM. You declare the stack in one HCL file, doze.hcl. Each service starts on its first connection and sleeps when nothing has used it for a while (2 minutes by default). doze is a desktop app (one window for every stack, a menu bar icon) and a CLI; both are the same binary. It is for local development, not production.

Key facts:
- Install: the app with `brew install --cask doze-dev/tap/doze` on macOS; deb and rpm packages on Linux. The CLI is the same binary. Running `doze` opens the app; every app action is also a command.
- doze.hcl has four kinds of block: `module <type> "<name>"` (an engine from the doze registry, e.g. `module postgres "db" { version = 18 }`), `app` (your own code), `service` (any other long-running program, e.g. mailpit) and `task` (runs to completion, e.g. a migration). `after = [task.migrate, module.db]` orders them; references such as `module.db.url` wire them. Root fields: `stack`, `doze`; `defaults { sleep = "2m"  names = true }`.
- Modules come only from the doze registry (registry.doze-dev.com for doze 0.2): postgres, valkey, kvrocks, ferret (FerretDB, MongoDB wire protocol), mariadb, temporal, kafka and aws. `aws` is one module with S3, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB, Lambda, EventBridge, KMS, SSM, Secrets Manager, STS and Step Functions. Anything else runs as your own `service` (`doze add <name> --as installed|container|download`). New modules are contributed by pull request to github.com/doze-dev/doze-modules.
- Modules are signed; the registry key is compiled into doze. doze.lock pins engine binaries, modules and downloads; commit it. Pins move only with `doze modules upgrade`.
- Names: with `names = true` each service is `<name>.<stack>.doze` on an address of its own, so every Postgres can use 5432. A front door serves apps on :80 and :443. One-time machine setup: `doze dns-setup` (undo with `--uninstall`); `doze trust` for an app's own https `domains`.
- States: awake, dozing, waking, asleep, crashing, failed, stopped. `sleep = "never"` or `doze pin` keeps a service awake; `doze off` keeps it stopped.
- Commands: `doze init`, `add`, `up` (`--last`, `--all`), `down`, `status`, `logs`, `wake`, `sleep`, `restart`, `reset`, `task`, `pin`, `on`, `off`, `url`, `env`, `run --env -- <cmd>`, `migrate` (Postgres majors), `lint`, `fmt`, `doctor`, `modules upgrade`. `--json` gives one envelope; exit codes are stable.
- Upgrading from doze 0.1: `process` is now `app`/`service`/`task`, `depends_on` is `after`, `idle_timeout` is `sleep`, `name` is `stack`, engine blocks are `module <type> "<name>"`.

## Start here

- [Install the app](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/start/install/): Install doze on a Mac or on Linux, open it once, and let it set up names for your services.
- [Your first stack](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/start/first-stack/): Open an example project in the app, bring it up, and watch each service wake.
- [Bring your own repo](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/start/your-repo/): Point doze at your own project, let it write a doze.hcl from what it finds, and bring it up.
- [How doze thinks](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/start/how-doze-thinks/): The four kinds of block, sleep and wake, names, and start order, in one page.

## The app

- [Library and stacks](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/library/): Home, the list of every stack on this machine, and how to add, start, stop and remove one.
- [Tiles, List, Map and Grid](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/views/): The four views of a stack's page, what each shows, and when to use which.
- [Inside a service](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/inside-a-service/): A service's own page, with how to reach it, why it is awake, its logs, its console, and a task's runs.
- [When something breaks](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/when-something-breaks/): What the app shows when a service crashes, a port is taken, or doze.hcl stops loading, and how to fix each.
- [⌘K and keys](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/keys/): The ⌘K palette, and every key the app answers to, page by page.
- [Menu bar and notifications](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/menu-bar/): The bat in the menu bar, what its menu offers, and when doze sends a notification.
- [Domains and HTTPS](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/domains/): Give an app a real name under a public TLD, served over https on your machine, so sign-in callbacks, cookies and tenant subdomains work locally.
- [Settings and Doctor](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/app/settings/): The app's settings, the machine's setup part by part, and Repair when a part is missing.

## doze.hcl

- [Apps](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/apps/): Declare your own code in doze.hcl, an API, a worker or a web front end, so doze starts it, restarts it and gives it a name.
- [Shared services](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/shared-services/): Add Postgres, Valkey, Kafka, AWS and the other registry modules to a stack, choose their versions, and keep them pinned.
- [Your own services](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/your-own-services/): Run a program that is not in the registry, such as mailpit, MongoDB or MinIO, as a service in your stack, from your PATH, a container or a download.
- [Tasks](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/tasks/): Run migrations, installs and seed scripts as tasks, before the apps that need them and again only when their files change.
- [Start order and readiness](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/start-order/): Say what each service waits for with after, and when it counts as ready with ready.
- [Sleep and wake](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/sleep/): How long services stay awake with nothing using them, how to change it, and how to keep one up or take one out.
- [Names and addresses](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/names/): How every service gets a name like postgres.larder.doze, how apps are served without a port, and what happens with names off.
- [References and env](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/references-and-env/): Pass one block's address to another by reference, set environment variables, and parameterise a stack with variables.
- [Splitting files](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/splitting-files/): Split a stack's doze.hcl across several files, and change a few settings on your machine only with an override file.
- [Teams and CI](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/hcl/teams-and-ci/): Share a stack with your team through two committed files, and run it in CI with stable output and exit codes.

## Services

- [Postgres](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/postgres/): Run a real PostgreSQL server, with its roles, schemas, grants and extensions declared in doze.hcl.
- [Valkey](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/valkey/): Run Valkey, the open-source Redis, as an in-memory cache any Redis client can use.
- [Kvrocks](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/kvrocks/): Run Kvrocks, the Redis protocol on disk, for keys that survive sleep and restarts without living in RAM.
- [FerretDB](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/ferretdb/): Run a MongoDB-compatible database that any Mongo driver, mongosh or Compass connects to.
- [MariaDB](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/mariadb/): Run MariaDB, the MySQL-compatible database, with its users and grants declared in doze.hcl.
- [Temporal](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/temporal/): Run a local Temporal server, with its Web UI and namespaces, for your workflow workers.
- [Kafka](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/kafka/): Run a single-node Kafka-protocol broker, with its topics declared in doze.hcl and a web console, without a JVM.
- [AWS](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/services/aws/): Run local AWS (S3, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB, Lambda and more) as one service, with buckets, queues and tables declared in doze.hcl.

## Guides

- [Microservices](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/microservices/): Run a stack of your own services in Go, Python and TypeScript, in order, beside the databases they use, from one doze.hcl.
- [Everyday workflows](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/workflows/): Start a stack, connect to it, read its logs, run a task, change doze.hcl and stop for the day, in the app or in a terminal.
- [Upgrading from 0.1](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/upgrading-from-0-1/): Every spelling doze 0.2 changed in doze.hcl and on the command line, and what to write instead.
- [Postgres major upgrades](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/postgres-upgrades/): Move a Postgres service's data from one major version to the next with doze migrate, keeping the old data until you are sure.
- [Files and storage](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/files-and-storage/): Where doze keeps binaries, data, logs and state, what to commit, and how to clean up.
- [Memory](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/memory/): What doze holds in memory when a stack is idle and while you work, measured, with how to measure it yourself.
- [Linux](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/linux/): Install doze on Linux, set up .doze names with systemd-resolved, and undo all of it.
- [Troubleshooting](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/troubleshooting/): What to do when a service crashes, a port is taken, a name does not resolve, an app is never ready, or doze.hcl does not load.
- [FAQ](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/guides/faq/): Short answers to the questions people ask about doze, with links to the pages that go further.

## Reference

- [CLI](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/cli/): Every doze command and flag, with the JSON envelope and exit codes for scripts.
- [doze.hcl](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/doze-hcl/): Every block and field doze.hcl takes, with its type, default and what it does.
- [Environment](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/environment/): Every environment variable doze reads, and the ones it sets for your commands and prints for your shell.
- [doze.lock](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/lockfile/): What doze.lock pins, field by field, and what changes it.
- [Binaries](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/binaries/): Where the engine binaries doze runs come from, how they are checked and pinned, and where they live on disk.
- [Postgres extensions](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/extensions/): Which Postgres extensions work out of the box, and how to install one that doesn't ship with Postgres.
- [Architecture](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/reference/architecture/): How doze is built (the binary, the daemon, modules, names and the app) and which repo holds each part.

## Contribute to the registry

- [How the registry works](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/contribute/registry/): Where doze gets modules, what the signed index holds, where the key lives, and what a module must meet to get in.
- [Propose a module](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/contribute/propose/): Ask for a new engine in the doze registry, and agree on it before anyone writes code.
- [Write it in doze-modules](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/contribute/write/): Lay out a new module in doze-modules, implement the driver, describe it, and register it in the four places the repo checks.
- [Test it](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/contribute/test/): Run the same checks doze-modules CI runs on your module, from unit tests to acceptance against the real backend.
- [Submit and release](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/contribute/submit/): Open the pull request, pass the checklist, and follow your module from the merge to a signed release in the registry.

## Why doze

- [Why doze](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/why/doze/): The problem doze solves, what it does instead of a VM or always-on services, and when it is the wrong tool.
- [Native processes vs containers](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/why/not-containers/): Why the services next to your editor should be processes on your machine, not containers in a VM, and what containers are still for.
- [Why HCL](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/why/hcl/): Why doze.hcl is HCL and not YAML or JSON, argued from what doze does with it.
- [Alternatives](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/why/alternatives/): What docker-compose, Testcontainers, LocalStack, Nix, Tilt and brew services are good at, and when to pick them over doze.
- [The trust model](https://doze-dev.com/docs/doze/why/trust/): How doze checks every module and binary it downloads, what doze.lock pins, and what the signatures do not prove.
